sources.entry: My Claude Code Setup by Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna - A ready-to-fork Claude Code template for academics using LaTeX/Beamer + R. Multi-agent review, quality gates, adversarial QA, and replication protocols. Great use of orchestration patterns and great documentation.

summary.one_liner: A ready-to-fork Claude Code template for academic work (LaTeX/Beamer slides, Quarto, R, papers and replication packages) that bundles specialized review agents, skills, rules and quality gates.
summary.what_it_does: The repo is a forkable configuration for Claude Code aimed at academics, with a CLAUDE.md, rules, skills, agents, and hooks. The README lists 18 agents (e.g., proofreader, slide-auditor, pedagogy-reviewer, r-reviewer, claim-verifier, methods-referee) and around 61 skills covering slide compilation, Quarto rendering, adversarial critic-fixer QA loops, peer-review simulation for manuscripts, literature review, data analysis, and replication packaging. A backtest.sh script runs a set of gates (skill integrity, link checks, staleness, hook battery, and others), and an optional pre-commit hook enforces a quality score threshold of 80 on commits. Scores of 80, 90 and 95 are used as commit, PR and excellence thresholds. Several hooks guard git operations such as destructive resets and dirty-tree merges. The README also covers verification skills (/verify-claims, /audit-reproducibility) and workflow patterns for R, Stata and Python projects.
use_cases: Creating and reviewing Beamer or Quarto lecture slides
Simulated peer review and revision of academic manuscripts
End-to-end R data analysis with reproducibility checks
Literature review and research ideation with Claude Code
Checking paper claims against script output
how_to_run: Fork the repository on GitHub and clone your fork
Run claude in the project directory
Paste the starter prompt from the guide, filled in with your project details
Optionally verify with /compile-latex HelloWorld and /deploy HelloWorld
notable: Ten-gate backtest suite plus a pre-commit hook that enforces quality scoring on every commit
Adversarial QA where a critic and fixer agent loop until no new issues appear
Peer-review pipeline with editor, domain and methods referees, and variance reporting across sampled dispositions
Guard hooks that block destructive git commands and writes to the gate-defining config files
Path-scoped rules that load only when relevant files are being edited
caveats: The README states that the template is extracted from one author's production PhD course workflow and that the full guide is needed for details
Many skills and features are tied to Claude Code versions and model tiers, and the README notes they change over time
Guard hooks are described as textual tripwires rather than locks, and the README says they can be bypassed through several channels
